The QB pressure sensitivity primitive isolates the degradation in EPA when a QB is pressured, computed as the difference between EPA per dropback in clean pockets versus pressured situations. This requires precise alignment of nflverse data sources—specifically pbp and ftn_charting—to ensure accurate labeling of pressured plays. The primitive assumes that EPA is a valid measure of QB performance and that clean pocket EPA is a reliable baseline. Null guards prevent unreliable estimates when sample sizes are too small. The line stress index computes a residual from a linear model predicting pressure rate based on blitz rate. It captures how much a line’s pressure generation exceeds what would be expected given its blitz exposure. This relies on pfr_advstats for team-week level pressure and blitz counts, and requires a minimum dataset size for regression stability. Both primitives are vulnerable to data quality issues such as incomplete joins or mislabeled charting, which could introduce bias. The stress-test reveals that FTN pressure is subjective and that EPA does not adjust for opponent strength, limiting interpretability.
